headline: This law directs the Department of Homeland Security to create a process for reporting security flaws in its systems and a pilot bug bounty program, and sets new federal rules for managing supply chain risks in buying technology.
what_it_does: DHS must publish a policy for anyone to report security weaknesses in its information systems, and it must set up a process for fixing those weaknesses. The law also creates a bug bounty pilot program in which outside individuals and companies are temporarily allowed to find and report flaws in exchange for pay. Separately, it creates a Federal Acquisition Security Council and sets standards that federal agencies must follow to assess and reduce risks when buying certain technology and equipment.

who_it_affects.group: Security researchers and other individuals who find software or system flaws
who_it_affects.how: They may be authorized to search for and report vulnerabilities in DHS systems under the bug bounty pilot and can receive compensation for valid reports.
DHS must create and publish a vulnerability reporting policy, build a remediation process, and run a bug bounty pilot through its Office of the Chief Information Officer.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that buy technology and equipment
who_it_affects.how: They must assess supply chain risks, use mitigation strategies, and follow exclusion and removal orders when acquiring covered articles.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that sell technology or equipment to the federal government
who_it_affects.how: They may be excluded from or removed from federal purchasing if their products are identified as posing supply chain risks under the new rules.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on December 21, 2018; the summary does not list other specific effective dates or deadlines for the reporting policy, remediation process, or bug bounty pilot.
